hawkish.title: Oct 28 FOMC hold on a 10-2 vote: Cook and Hammack dissent for +25bp
hawkish.summary: The Committee held 3.75-4.00% but two voters wanted a quarter-point hike now; the statement keeps 'inflation remains elevated' and calls activity 'expanding at a strong pace'.
hawkish.reason: Two dissents in favour of an immediate hike show the hawkish wing is not waiting for December; together with unchanged 'inflation remains elevated' language this kept the bar for a December move low rather than signalling a pause.
hawkish.market_validation: Kalshi Dec 25bp-Hike leg 0.79 at the 14:00 ET hourly close -> 0.80-0.81 in the 15:00-16:00 ET hours on 28 Oct (76.9k contracts in the decision hour).

hawkish.title: October payrolls +165,000, unemployment 4.1%: no cooling ahead of 9 December
hawkish.summary: Total nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000 against a 65,000 consensus; the unemployment rate fell to 4.1% from 4.2% and average hourly earnings rose 0.4% m/m (+3.1% y/y). August and September were revised up a combined 84,000 (August +133k to +186k, September +29k to +60k). Gains were led by professional and business services (+70,000), health care (+42,000) and transportation and warehousing (+25,000); participation edged up to 61.9% from 61.8%.

data.delta_label: +100k vs consensus; +84k of upward revisions; unemployment -0.1pp

hawkish.reason: The last payroll report before the 9 December decision beat consensus by 100,000 with 84,000 of upward revisions and a falling unemployment rate, so the slack argument for holding is weaker than it was on 4 November. The gains are broad (business services, health care, transport) rather than one sector, and wages at +0.4% m/m keep the inflation side of the mandate in play.
hawkish.market_validation: Kalshi Dec 25bp-Hike leg 0.64/0.65 (mid 0.645) at the 5 Nov close (23:00 ET) -> 0.78/0.79 (mid 0.785) in the 09:00 ET candle on 6 Nov, +14.0pp across the 08:30 ET release on 68,547 contracts; Polymarket's 25bp leg went 0.655 (5 Nov 23:00 ET) -> 0.785 (6 Nov 09:00 ET), and Reuters reported bets rising 'to 78% following the data from 70% earlier'. The print reversed the 5 November sell-off rather than setting a new high: the leg had closed 4 November at 0.79/0.80.

hawkish.title: Hammack: policy 'will need to move to a restrictive stance' to get inflation back to 2%
hawkish.summary: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack - a 2026 voter and one of the two October dissents for +25bp - said in panel remarks at the SNB and Its Watchers conference in Zurich that she expects 'that monetary policy will need to move to a restrictive stance to bring inflation back to 2 percent in a timely manner'.

data.actual: "monetary policy will need to move to a restrictive stance to bring inflation back to 2 percent in a timely manner"
data.previous: 28 Oct: dissented for +25bp while the Committee held
data.delta_label: explicit call for a restrictive stance

hawkish.reason: One of the two votes for an immediate hike is now saying policy has to become restrictive, not merely less accommodative - a stronger formulation than the Committee's own statement - which keeps the hawkish wing's bar for December low.
hawkish.market_validation: No hawkish repricing on the day and none credited here: the Kalshi Dec 25bp-Hike leg fell from 0.79/0.80 (09:00 ET) to 0.64/0.65 by 17:00 ET on 5 Nov, then recovered to 0.78/0.79 in the 6 Nov payroll hour, so the session's 15pp swing is not attributable to her remarks.

hawkish.title: Waller: leaning to a December hike, 50bp 'should be considered' if core CPI is 0.3%
hawkish.summary: Governor Christopher Waller said in London that he is leaning toward a 25bp increase on 9 December even if October inflation improves, and that core CPI around 0.3% would justify weighing a 50bp move: 'Hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take.'

data.actual: "I am leaning toward supporting an increase in our policy rate of 25 basis points at the FOMC's December meeting ... I believe a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered"
data.previous: no size guidance from a Governor earlier in the cycle

hawkish.reason: A Governor pre-committing to a December hike and naming the data threshold for an upsized move removes the wait-and-see option for the Committee and makes 25bp the floor; the 50bp branch is live as long as core CPI prints 0.3%.
hawkish.market_validation: Kalshi Dec 25bp-Hike leg 0.80/0.81 (mid 0.805) at 04:00 ET -> 0.88/0.89 (mid 0.885) at 05:00 ET on 10 Nov, +8.0pp on 28,077 contracts; the >25bp leg (H26) went 0.01/0.02 -> 0.02/0.03 in the same hour on 748,703 contracts and 0.04/0.06 by 06:00 ET.

hawkish.title: October CPI +0.4% m/m, core +0.3% a third straight month, above consensus
hawkish.summary: Headline CPI +0.4% m/m after +0.6% in September and core +0.3% for the third consecutive month (August, September, October); shelter +0.3%, energy +0.7%, gasoline +1.0%, food +0.5%. Both headline and core came in 0.1pp above the Dow Jones consensus (0.3% / 0.2%). BLS published no 12-month change: October 2025 survey data were never collected because of the lapse in appropriations.

data.delta_label: +0.1pp on headline and core; third straight 0.3% core

hawkish.reason: Core inflation has now run at 0.3% for three months with the pipeline hot behind it (October PPI final demand +6.5% y/y and core +0.5% m/m on 13 November), which is exactly the reading Waller named as the trigger for considering 50bp; it keeps a 25bp December increase as the floor rather than the ceiling.
hawkish.market_validation: At the 08:30 ET print the Kalshi >25bp leg (H26) went from 0.05/0.06 (mid 0.055) at 08:00 ET to 0.10/0.11 (mid 0.105) at 09:00 ET and 0.12/0.14 at 10:00 ET on 345,470 contracts, +5.0pp, while the 25bp leg slipped from 0.86/0.87 to 0.85/0.86 as the size mix shifted.

hawkish.title: Jefferson: October data 'consistent with well above-target inflation', inflation is the signal
hawkish.summary: Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said data since the October meeting show activity and the labour market broadly solid, that October price data remain 'consistent with well above-target inflation', and that he sees 'the trajectory of inflation as providing the more important signal' for the stance; further adjustments should follow 'carefully examining trends in the data'. He cited September PCE inflation of 3.6% and core 3.1%.

data.actual: "The trajectory of inflation as providing the more important signal ... data received so far for October remains consistent with well above-target inflation"
data.previous: 28 Oct: voted with the majority to hold

hawkish.reason: The Vice Chair has put the reaction function on inflation alone at a point when the labour market has stopped cooling (October payrolls +165k, unemployment 4.1%), which supports a December hike while stopping short of committing to one - the dovish counterweight is that he still frames any move as data-dependent.
hawkish.market_validation: unverified (the remarks landed after the 13 Nov cash close; the 13 Nov 09:00 ET candle move belongs to the 08:30 PPI print, not to this speech)

dovish.title: Warsh: no forward guidance, 'I don't believe in prejudging meetings'
dovish.summary: Asked whether a December hike still has wide support, Warsh declined to guide, said the period ahead is 'information rich' and that inflation compensation is 'going in the right way' and expectations have 'gone the right way too'.

data.previous: Sep SEP: 2026 median 4.1% (full range 3.9-4.4), i.e. the dots implied one more hike

dovish.summary: Nominal PCE +0.5% but real PCE less than +0.1% m/m (Aug +0.5%); real DPI -0.3% (Aug 0.0%); saving rate 3.8%.

hawkish.summary: The Bank lifted its CPI path: inflation 'expected to rise to about 3.5% by the end of the year' and to average 3% in 2027 (MPR Table: 2.9% in 2026 and 3.1% in 2027, against July's 2.5% and 2.0%), coming back to 2% only by the middle of 2028. 'There could be a need to increase the policy rate further.'

data.actual: +25bp to 2.50%; CPI about 3.5% by end-2026, 3% average 2027 (MPR 2.9% / 3.1%)
data.forecast: +25bp: CORRA OIS ~96% (BlueGamma, page stamped 08:27:48 ET), Polymarket 85.3% (09:08 ET) pre-release

hawkish.reason: The Bank now projects inflation at about 3.5% by year-end and around 3% through 2027, kept an explicit tightening bias, and attributed the revision to energy prices it expects to stay higher for longer, so December stays a live meeting. The hike itself was priced (85-96%), so there is no surprise credit.
hawkish.market_validation: Kalshi BoC Dec 25bp-Hike leg 0.47/0.49 before the release, first traded 0.46 at 09:45 ET and fell to 0.33-0.35 within 12 minutes, rebounded to 0.39-0.40 by mid-afternoon and sat at 0.37 on 29 Oct (about -11c net from the pre-release mid), so the market read the release as less hawkish for December than the projection alone implies. Post-decision swaps ~60% for a December hike (Bloomberg data via The Globe and Mail, 28 Oct) - secondary, not independently verified.

hawkish.title: Growth outlook upgraded: Q2 3.3%, Q3 ~2%, 'somewhat stronger' than July
hawkish.summary: Growth picked up through mid-year and the projection is 'somewhat stronger' than July: 1% in 2026, 2% in 2027 and 2028; Q2 3.3%, Q3 indicators point to about 2%.
hawkish.reason: Q3 growth came in 'stronger than expected in the July Report' and the rebound is expected to resume in 2027 on investment, exports and fiscal measures, which weakens the slack argument for holding.

dovish.title: Macklem: 'we will proceed carefully', core near 2%, slack remains
dovish.summary: Opening statement set out the hold case: core inflation close to 2%, CPI ex-gasoline 2.2%, excess supply, and new US tariffs expected to slow Q4 growth; decisions 'one meeting at a time'.

data.actual: "There could be a need to raise the policy rate further, but given the uncertainties, we will proceed carefully."

dovish.reason: Governing Council explicitly weighed a hold and kept core inflation and slack in the argument; with growth expected to slow in Q4 on tariffs, a second move needs energy pass-through to show up first.
dovish.market_validation: Kalshi BoC Dec 25bp-Hike leg 0.46 -> 0.33-0.35 in the 12 minutes after the 09:45 ET release, 0.39-0.40 after the 10:30 ET press conference, 0.37 on 29 Oct; Polymarket 35.7% hike on 29 Oct. Thin book (~24k contracts).

dovish.title: August GDP flat at 0.0% (0.2% expected); September advance -0.1%
dovish.summary: Real GDP by industry was unchanged in August for a second straight month (9 of 20 sectors up; services -0.1%, goods +0.1%). StatCan's advance estimate points to -0.1% in September, leaving Q3 tracking about 1.2% annualised against the Bank's 2% projection.

data.actual: 0.0% m/m Aug; advance -0.1% Sep; Q3 tracking ~1.2% annualised (0.3% q/q)
data.delta_label: -0.2pp vs consensus; Q3 tracking ~0.8pp below the BoC projection

dovish.reason: The Bank hiked on 28 Oct on a growth upgrade (Q3 about 2%); a flat August followed by a negative September advance puts Q3 near 1.2% annualised, which restores the slack argument for holding in December. The surprise credit for the turn sits with the 6 Nov LFS (boc-d6), so this entry is scored 2 rather than 3.
dovish.market_validation: Kalshi BoC Dec 25bp-Hike leg 0.38 previous close -> 0.35 last trade 07:40:06 ET and a 0.35/0.36 book at 09:15 ET, while the hold leg traded 0.65 at 09:00:43 ET; the books are thin, so attribution to this release is not verified.

dovish.title: October LFS: employment -4,700, unemployment 6.7%, wages slow to 2.2%
dovish.summary: Employment was little changed in October (-4,700; 0.0%) against a +13.6k consensus; the unemployment rate rose 0.2pp to 6.7% (6.5% expected) as more people searched for work, and the employment rate fell 0.1pp to 60.5%, a third consecutive monthly decline. Average hourly wages slowed to 2.2% y/y from 2.3%. Wholesale and retail trade lost 29,000 while construction (+16,000) and educational services (+15,000) added.
dovish.reason: A second consecutive employment decline plus a rising unemployment rate leaves the labour market softer than the Bank assumed when it hiked on 28 October, and wage growth easing to 2.2% removes the pass-through argument for a second move in December. It does not argue for a cut - employment is still 17,000 above its year-ago level - so the weight stays modest.
dovish.market_validation: Kalshi BoC Dec 25bp-Hike leg 0.36/0.37 (mid 0.365) at the 5 Nov close -> 0.29/0.31 (mid 0.30) at 09:14 ET on 6 Nov, -6.5c across the 08:30 ET release; Polymarket 40.5% on 4 Nov -> 30.2% at 09:13 ET. Normalised Kalshi hike probability 40.8% -> 30.0%.

dovish.title: October CPI 3.1% with ex-energy down to 2.0%: the pass-through the Bank hiked against is not showing
dovish.summary: CPI +3.1% y/y in October, matching September, and +0.2% m/m (0.2% seasonally adjusted); CPI excluding energy slowed to 2.0% from 2.1%. Shelter 1.4%, food purchased from stores 2.0%, transportation 8.9% on gasoline; cell phone plans fell and rent growth slowed. The print sits below the Bank's 'about 3.5% by the end of the year' path.

dovish.reason: The December case rests on energy costs spreading into other prices; three weeks after the hike the ex-energy measure is falling rather than rising and headline is below the Bank's year-end projection, which argues for waiting rather than a second consecutive increase.

notes:
Snapshot assembled at 09:20 ET on Monday 16 November 2026, about an hour after the October Canadian CPI and before Fed Chair Warsh's scheduled 12:00 ET remarks. Both books repriced hard since the 9 November snapshot: the Fed December hike leg went from 76.8% to 94.6% on Kalshi and the BoC leg from 26.9% to 46.5%. Every pricing block carries the source's own stamp and both venues were pulled for this snapshot rather than reused: the two Kalshi ladder responses returned HTTP Date Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:17:39 GMT (09:17:39 ET), and the Polymarket event responses are stamped 09:15:55 ET (Fed) and 09:17:39 ET (BoC) with the event objects updated at 09:15:09 and 09:16:56 ET.

Fed: the move is Waller's, not drift. On 10 November, before the CPI, the December 25bp leg went 0.80/0.81 -> 0.88/0.89 and the >25bp leg 0.01/0.02 -> 0.02/0.03 in the 05:00 ET hour; the 08:30 ET CPI then took the >25bp leg to 0.10/0.11 while the 25bp leg slipped to 0.85/0.86 - the print bought size, not direction. October PPI on 13 November (+0.3% m/m but +6.5% y/y, the fastest since November 2022, core +0.5% m/m) and Jefferson's 13 November remarks held it there. CME FedWatch, read second-hand because cmegroup.com refuses this host: 67% on 5 November, 100% on 12 November, 95% for 25bp and 5% for 50bp this morning.

BoC: the repricing is not today's CPI. The Kalshi hike leg sat at 0.37-0.39 through 11 November, went to 0.42/0.43 at 14:00 ET on 12 November and 0.50-0.55 by the 13 November morning with no Canadian release behind it; the 10 November summary of deliberations ('there could be a need to increase the policy rate further', 'uncertainty did not mean inaction') and spillover from US rates are the only candidates, and the deliberations are not scored separately because boc-h7 already carries that sentence. Today's CPI trimmed 2pp off the hike leg (mid 0.485 -> 0.465).

Driver list: five new entries - fed-h17 (Waller, 10 November), fed-h18 (October CPI), fed-h19 (Hammack, 5 November), fed-h20 (Jefferson, 13 November) and boc-d7 (October CPI) - and four retirements: fed-h10 (28 October press-conference growth/inflation read), fed-h11 (September PCE), fed-h12 (Q3 GDP) and fed-h13 (October ISM). The retirements lower the score rather than raise it: keeping all four would put the decayed Fed total near 17 on a ±10 gauge. Nothing is lost from the record - fed-h9 carries the 10-2 vote and the statement language, fed-h20 quotes the September PCE figures (3.6%, core 3.1%) that fed-h11 scored, and October PCE is not published yet.

Prior review: the 9 November pm-review.json is REVISE with two major must_fix findings and both are closed. (1) fed-h16 no longer claims a 0.79/0.80 close on 5 November or a -1.0pp payroll move: it states 0.64/0.65 at the 5 November close, 0.78/0.79 in the 6 November 09:00 ET candle (+14.0pp on 68,547 contracts), Polymarket 0.655 -> 0.785 and Reuters' '78% ... from 70%', and the conclusion now reads that the beat reversed the 5 November sell-off back to the 4 November level instead of adding nothing. (2) The claim of no Fed communication since the 15 October speech list is gone: Hammack is fed-h19 on the Cleveland Fed release, Jefferson is fed-h20, and every Fed communication since 28 October is accounted for - 28 October statement and press conference (fed-h9, fed-d7), Hammack 5 November (fed-h19), Waller 10 November (fed-h17), Barr on AI and inequality 12 November (no policy content, not scored), Jefferson 13 November (fed-h20). Both minors are done as well: both venues were re-pulled on fresh stamps, and the implied-move arithmetic now subtracts the cut legs (0.863 x 25 + 0.083 x 50 - 0.005 x 25 - 0.005 x 50 = 25.4bp) instead of adding them.

Totals: Fed base +14 clamps to +10 (strong hike lean) and the decayed sum is +13.0, so the rendered marker is pinned at the top of the ±10 gauge - the honest reading of a 94.6% priced hike, and there is no room left on the axis for the extra weight. BoC base -3 / decayed -2.5 (hold; mean |weight| 2.17 over 6 drivers). The BoC driver total sits on the hold side while the December book is a near coin flip at 46.5% hike: the board scores two soft labour prints and today's ex-energy deceleration, the market carries an oil and pass-through premium the Bank itself raised on 10 November. No averaging and no divergence badge - the pricing leader is still hold. Calendar: the two released CPI rows are dropped, leaving 30 November Canadian Q3 GDP, 4 December payrolls on both sides and the two 9 December decisions, with forecast strings taken from today's ladders. BoC communication since the decision, all checked: Macklem's 3 November House of Commons and 5 November Senate statements (restatements of 28 October, not scored), the 10 November deliberations, and the 5 November framework renewal (2% target inside the 1-3% band to 2031, no operational change).
